watch.label: Riders of Destiny (1933), Lone Star Productions, dir. Robert N. Bradbury

editorial:
Riders of Destiny is a 1933 Lone Star Productions western directed by Robert N. Bradbury, with John Wayne as 'Singin' Sandy' Saunders, a gunman who turns out to be a Secret Service agent sent to investigate a land swindle. It is an early Wayne starring role, which is what makes it attractive to documentary makers, western compilations and Wayne-centred projects.

The rights trap is that the renewal check is not finished here. The 1960-1962 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes were located but their renewal sections were not fully searched, and no Copyright Office catalog search was completed, so the print cannot be called free yet. Separately, an AI-colorized, upscaled 2021 version circulates on the Internet Archive. Whatever that version adds is a separate question from the 1933 images, so check which copy you are taking.
faq: Is Riders of Destiny (1933) safe to reuse?
Not yet confirmed. The renewal volumes for 1960-1962 were not fully searched, and the Copyright Office catalog was not searched. Finish both checks before relying on the print.
Can I use the colorized 4K version?

Treat it with caution. A colorized, AI-upscaled copy adds new material that may be protected separately from the underlying 1933 film. Working from a plain black-and-white transfer avoids that question.
